cells.tense: Right now the light is simply on, and you are the one standing in it.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Look back at the last few times something you cared for came through, and write the shape they share on a single line. Change nothing. Read what you wrote.
cells.core:
You know how to let a thing become itself. You tend what is growing without pulling at it, and what you care for comes out whole. That is a steady hand, and it isn't a technique you're running — it's what you do when you're not arranging anything.

The next stretch asks something more specific of you. Don't tend harder; look at how you tend. Take the last few times something you cared for came through and find the shape running through them, the waiting you keep doing on purpose. You'll likely see it isn't laziness. It's the method. Once you can see the method moving in your own hands, you can pick it up deliberately instead of only having it.
cells.sheetLine: You know how to let a thing become itself.
cells.place: where what is growing is tended

cells.tense: Soon you will be steering every outcome before the growth has started to move.
cells.act: leave it undecided a while longer
cells.ask: Take what you're currently driving toward a result and hold it open for seven days. No plan for where it lands. No verdict this week.
cells.core:
You're tending, and it has quietly turned into driving. You've settled what the thing should become, and now you're working out how to make it happen — the making is being asked to do something the growing wasn't. Underneath the arranging, the light was already there before you had a plan for it.

Keep one thing undecided this week. One. Don't lay the path, don't settle what it means yet. If it feels like nothing is happening, that's the point — undecided isn't empty. What you find when you stop steering is what wanted to arrive with no help from you, and the room to receive it when it does.
cells.sheetLine: You've settled what it should be before it's grown.
cells.place: where what is growing is tended

cells.tense: A door closed behind you, and you are still at its threshold.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Credit a finished piece of work as done, plainly, in your own head. Then pick what gets tended from here, chosen rather than drifted into.
cells.core:
The thing is finished. It's real and it's behind you, and some part of you won't take it. Not modesty exactly — more that you waited so long to feel done that you keep hovering where the room has already moved past. The skill is here. The dimming is what's off.

Count a finished thing, in your own head, plainly. Then choose — pick what gets tended from here, in the same voice you'd use for anything true. Direction is what refills this. Say 'this, not that' and mean it, and the current comes back on. Tending gets warmer once it has an object.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished, and some part of you won't take it.

cells.tense: The light is on in this room, and you are crossing it without turning your head.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Three times today, catch what arrived with no work from you — the message, the small yes, the unplanned second. Note it plainly, nothing added, then go on.
cells.core:
You already give things what they need to come through. Patient with what's still forming, easy about timing, waiting on purpose. It works — you just don't count it as yours. That care is happening in a room where the light is yours and you keep walking past the switch.

Three times today, catch one thing that arrived with no work from you — the message, the small yes, the unplanned second. Note it plainly, nothing added, then go on with the day. You're not being asked to feel good about it. Only to see the turn as it happens. Seeing it is the whole practice; the caring was not the problem.
cells.sheetLine: The light in this room is yours. Turn your head.
cells.place: where what is growing is tended
